replication.target_description: Candidate target: first MANOVA comparing latent CU profiles on nine clustering indicators (anxiety, three CU facets, five childhood maltreatment subtypes), male-identified undergraduate participants aged 18–24. The broad supplied description and p. 13 locator do not uniquely distinguish this test from the separate PTSS and total-CU/total-maltreatment MANOVAs.

n.sample_role: Analytic male-identified participants in the clustering-indicator MANOVA; test-specific analytic n not explicitly established. The quoted 546 is the entire retained sample, not this test n.
n.exclusions: Study exclusions: invalid responses/failed more than 50% attention checks (n = 157), age over 24 (n = 17), and gender other than male/female or no response (n = 4). Test-specific missing-data exclusions not documented.

and females. This is inconsistent with one previous study (Kimonis et al.,

Source follow-up: Published 2022 article; title, authors and DOI match the assigned reference. Rendered PDF pages 7, 9, 11, 13 and 16 inspected. The first MANOVA is retained as a candidate, not a uniquely verified target: supplied p. 13 is discussion, and the neutral description does not identify an outcome set. target_match remains null. F and p come from the same candidate test. The rendered published p. 898 itself prints p < 001 (without a decimal), and Wilks’ Lambda = 02 / 05; these are not OCR-only losses. The p field preserves literal 001, not an inferred correction to .001, and is not numerically verified. The candidate F value is visually verified, but its match to the intended audit effect remains uncertain. No analytic n was calculated from group sizes, percentages, degrees of freedom or the overall sample. Success is a low-confidence mapping of the authors’ explicit somewhat-consistent CU-facet account and inconsistent neglect account to mixed; it is not inferred from statistical significance, nor specific to an identified omnibus target. Original side is an unassigned placeholder.
